newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks continue record run to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks continue record run to end higher.

text.p: Swiss shares for the first time closed above 4,300 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), continuing their latest four-day record run, despite profit taking in the second half of the session.
"It's normal that we see a correction after the market rose nine percent in January," a dealer said.
There was some insecurity in the market in connection with the U.S. FOMC meeting, eventhough the possibility of a U.S. interest rate hike seemed very small.
"A rate increase would be a major surprise," a dealer said.
The blue-chip SMI ended 9.0 points higher, or 0.21 percent, at 4,305.5. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 7.25 points, or 0.26 percent, to 2,750.03.
Roche certificates ended with a loss of 155 francs at 12,130 after a high of 12,380. A dealer said Roche's takeover of U.S. flavour firm Tastemaker led to some uncertainty.
Investors who were hoping Roche would announce a major merger or a spin-off may have been disappointed, he added.
Major banks generally outperformed the market.
Group, UBS and SBC said they would set up a fund of 100 million francs for holocaust victims.
"This bodes well for Switzerland as a financial center," a trader noted.
UBS bearers added 17 francs to 1,219. SBC jumped six francs to 274. Credit Suisse Group firmed 0.75 francs to 147.75. Insurers were generally also higher.
Novartis, which gave details about the imminent spin-off of Ciba Specialty Chemicals, also edged up. The registereds were up three francs to 1,659. Clariant and Ems lost ground.
Alusuisse profited from a positive study, dealers said. The registered shares rose 20 francs to 1,200.
ABB, Holderbank, SMH, Sulzer, Swissair and Adia were among the day's losers. Adia gave up nine francs, or more than two percent, to 387 francs.
